candidate_workflows.description: Use this workflow when a runtime can see both an endpoint-specific credential and a generic compatibility credential, and an authentication failure suggests that the generic credential was selected for the wrong endpoint. First inspect every resolution entry point, then align the precedence expressions, and finally test both the conflict and fallback states. Anti-goals are to remove the generic fallback, change base-URL or provider selection, or assume that a variable-name ordering is correct for arbitrary custom endpoints without a separate endpoint-aware policy decision. This workflow is not applicable until the endpoint-specific and fallback credential roles are known.
candidate_workflows.name: repair-provider-specific-credential-precedence-with-fallback

workflow_graph.goal: Make credential selection deterministic at the provider boundary so the selected endpoint receives its intended credential without removing compatibility fallback behavior.

episode.before: [E1,E2,E3,E6,E8,E9] At the first parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, the CLI constructor initialized its cached api_key as explicit_api_key, OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, while _resolve_openrouter_runtime used explicit_api_key, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then an empty fallback. When both environment keys were available for an OpenRouter request, the OpenAI key won the OR chain and could be sent to OpenRouter, producing an authentication failure. episode.title: Resolve endpoint-specific credential precedence before generic fallback (#289)

evidence_units.claim: Issue #289 reports that when OPENAI_API_KEY from the shell environment and OPENROUTER_API_KEY configured for the selected runtime coexist, a request sent to OpenRouter carries the OpenAI credential and fails; unsetting OPENAI_API_KEY makes the request work.

An issue comment identifies two wrong resolution locations, cli.py:850 and hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:77-78, where OPENAI_API_KEY is checked before OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and links the regression-fix PR.

The pinned ref is merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a; GitHub metadata identifies first parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, second parent 60532361583b9dd0b4bd3f0e6b2755c9e1cfd41e, and the commit message states that OPENROUTER_API_KEY is resolved before OPENAI_API_KEY in all code paths.
The cli.py diff changes the cached API-key expression from explicit_api_key or OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY to explicit_api_key or OPENROUTER_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY.

The hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py diff changes _resolve_openrouter_runtime from explicit_api_key, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, empty to explicit_api_key, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, empty.
In the first-parent implementation, _resolve_openrouter_runtime is the shared runtime provider resolver and its pre-change api_key chain checks OPENAI_API_KEY before OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
At the pinned ref, _resolve_openrouter_runtime retains explicit and base-URL/provider behavior but returns the API key from the reordered OPENROUTER_API_KEY-before-OPENAI_API_KEY chain.

The pinned CLI _ensure_runtime_credentials function calls resolve_runtime_provider with the requested provider and explicit overrides, rejects empty credentials, updates the CLI's resolved provider/base URL/API key, and _init_agent passes those values into AIAgent.

The pinned gateway runtime entry point calls the shared resolver and forwards api_key, base_url, provider, and api_mode to gateway-created agent instances, so the shared precedence change reaches a second runtime entry point.

The pinned test file adds test_openrouter_key_takes_priority_over_openai_key, forces OpenRouter resolution, clears base-URL overrides, sets both keys, and asserts that the resolved API key is the OpenRouter key.
The pinned test file adds test_openai_key_used_when_no_openrouter_key, removes OPENROUTER_API_KEY while setting OPENAI_API_KEY, and asserts that the OpenAI key remains the fallback.

PR #295 describes the two regression tests and declares that all existing provider-resolution tests pass (7/7); this is a PR-declared validation result rather than an independently observed CI artifact.
The inspected GitHub metadata returned no commit statuses and no workflow runs for the pinned merge commit, so independent CI confirmation is unavailable in this episode.

A later issue comment raises an unresolved concern that variable-name priority may be wrong for custom endpoints and mentions an environment variable that is present but empty; the pinned implementation and tests do not establish an endpoint-aware or empty-value policy.

Comparing the first parent with the pinned merge ref reports exactly three changed files—cli.py, hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py, and tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py—with 34 additions and 2 deletions.
